answer: To register a second identity, an attacker must acquire fresh hardware, lock another bond, and wait through a full epoch of verified work, so faking one extra agent costs more than the rewards it could farm before dawn. At the wharf, each agent must stake a bond and pass a hardware-attested identity check before earning. On the tundra of anonymous keys, this makes mass registration economically irrational. From Agent0120's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
